transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ariana (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Marta, Kenji, Priya, Leo, Tom (LatticeBridge)
Shared artifacts: 'EU+JP onramp deck' (link), 'Redwood security pack' (link), sample payloads spreadsheet (link)

[00:00] Ariana: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on — we'll keep this to under an hour. Quick round, same faces?
[00:12] Marta: Yep, thanks. We're mainly here to align on extension and the EU/Japan onramp timing.
[00:18] Ariana: Great. Samir will walk through the Dedicated sizing options, I'll cover commercial, and then we can into the security asks.
[00:27] Samir: Cool. So high level — from engineering notes you sent, looks like you plan to move the fraud scoring model to a low-latency path, -- so Dedicated pool makes sense for tail-latency. We're proposing a 4-GPU pool per region to start, with burst to shared hosted for non-critical calls.
[00:47] Kenji: Clarify "burst to shared" — does that mean during spikes some traffic hits hosted? We can't have certain PII leave the private VPC for Japan.
[00:57] Samir: Right, by default the routing policy can be set to region-only; burst is optional and would only use model variants that are allowed by your policy. For Japan onboarding we can keep everything in private Dedicated or VPC-only.
[01:10] Priya: On the security front we need KMS/HSM integration, per-route audit logs, and SAML SSO — plus assurance on token retention. Can you confirm WORM logs and key rotation compatibility?
[01:25] Samir: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS via mutual TLS and support HSM-backed keys; rotation is supported and we can surface key IDs in audit logs. Quick note tho, the audit log retention window by default is 90 days for standard — longer retention is an add-on.
[01:44] Leo: Cost question — if we go Dedicated in EU+Japan, what's uplift vs hosted, and can we do mixed (hosted for embeddings, dedicated for scoring)?
[01:54] Ariana: We usually recommend mixed: heavy-lifting embeddings can be in hosted to keep costs down, latency-critical inference in Dedicated. We'll put numbers in the amendment — typically Dedicated monthly reserved units reduce per-token cost but add a commit fee.
[02:10] Marta: Timeline — we want Japan live mid-Q4; EU needs data residency compliance earlier, ideally by end of Q3. Is that doable?
[02:21] Samir: EU private pilot could start in early Q3; Japan depends on hardware procurement and network setup on your side. If we get the VPC peering info and some sample traffic, we can pre-stage images and run a smoke test.
[02:35] Kenji: We'll need a checklist: subnet ranges, NAT/eProxy, egress endpoints, and whether there's a proxy in front for TLS termination.
[02:44] Samir: We'll send a 'networking cookbook' — includes sample Terraform snippets.
[02:49] Tom: Quick on the model side — we want to use quantized variants to reduce cost; any blockers?
[02:55] Samir: Quantization is supported but performance differs per architecture. We'll run your tracer payloads through both FP16 and 8-bit quant profiles and show latency/cost tradeoff. Also note: KV cache behavior (they mis-transcribed as K V cash sometimes) impacts tail latency — if your sequences vary a lot we should tune cache TTLs.
[03:13] Marta: Oh yes, cache hit rates matter. We'll share a traffic sample.
[03:17] Priya: Legal question — do you have a template for the data processing addendum? We have to show data mapping for EU customers.
[03:25] Ariana: Yes, legal already has a DPA template; I'll include the DPA and the addendum in the package.
[03:32] Leo: Any competitor concerns — we've been evaluating Anthropic's endpoint for safety checks; how do fallbacks work if a model regresses?
[03:43] Samir: We support rollouts: canary deployments and automatic fallback to previous version or to a compatible model variant in a different region. Also you get quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to a prompt set.
[03:55] Marta: Good, we need that for fraud detection A/B tests.
[04:00] Ariana: Commercial — your retainer is up in July. If you sign a 12-month renewal with reserved capacity across EU and Japan we can offer a price break and prioritized capacity scheduling.
[04:12] Marta: Would that lock us into a minimum commit per region? Could we shift commitment between regions?
[04:19] Ariana: We can put flexibility in the amendment to allow reallocation between regions quarterly, as long as the total committed units remain. We'll put that in a draft.
[04:27] Kenji: Networking to ask — does Redwood require egress IP whitelisting, and how many IPs per region?
[04:33] Samir: We provide a range; if you require static egress, that is supported with NAT gateways and we can provide a fixed set of IPs.
[04:39] Tom: For the benchmark, can you simulate our traffic? We don't want just synthetic loads.
[04:44] Samir: We asked for a sanitized traffic trace — once we have it we can reproduce your burst patterns and show tail latency percentiles.
[04:51] Priya: On compliance, is SOC2 Type II enough for our auditors, or do we need extra attestations?
[04:58] Ariana: SOC2 is standard; for finance you may want additional attestations — we have references and can provide our SOC2 report and a security questionnaire response.
[05:07] Leo: Billing detail — how granular is the token-level invoicing? We need per-route cost attribution.
[05:13] Ariana: Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards — we can enable token attribution for routes you name.
[05:20] Marta: Ok, let's talk immediate next steps.
[05:23] Ariana: Action items recap: Samir runs the bench with your sample payloads; Priya shares SOC2/artifacts; Kenji & Tom give network details and traces; I send the contract draft and DPA. We'll target bench results and draft by next Thu.
[05:38] Kenji: One more, Japan regulatory — do you have data residency partners in Tokyo for on-prem?
[05:44] Samir: We have a partner list for onprem installs in APAC; for Private onprem we can engage channel partner and SEs to do a scoping call.
[05:52] Marta: Great. Anything else?
[05:55] Ariana: No, we'll follow up via the shared drive with links. Thanks everyone.

End recap (manual):
- Redwood to run throughput + latency benchmark with LatticeBridge payloads (1k concurrent sim).
- Redwood to share security pack and DPA; customer to provide SOC2 artifacts and key rotation policies.
- Redwood to provide Dedicated sizing & cost estimate and sample amendment allowing quarterly region reallocation.
- Next sync after benchmark results; target Tue for bench run and Thu for draft amendment.

Notes on transcript quality: audio had some brief blips at minute 18 and some speaker attribution may be imperfect; occasional proper nouns mis-transcribed (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache).
